10:1: As for the disconnected letters at the beginning of the surahs, we have already discussed them at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah. Abu Ad-Dahha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the Almighty’s statement: Alif, Lam, Ra. It means: I am God, I see. Ad-Dahhak and others also said: These are the verses of the Wise Book. There is a blank space in the original, meaning: these are the verses of the clear, decisive Qur’an. Mujahid said: “Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the Wise Book.” Al-Hasan said: The Torah and the Psalms. Qatada said: These are the verses of the Book. He said: The books that came before the Qur’an. I do not know the reason or meaning of this statement. And His statement: Was it a wonder to the people? The verse. God the Almighty says, denouncing those who were amazed by the infidels at the sending of human messengers, as He the Almighty informed us about the past generations when they said: Are human beings guiding us? And Hud and Salih said to their al-Nas 114:Or do you wonder that a reminder has come to you from your Lord through a man from among you? And God the Almighty said, informing us about the infidels of Quraysh that they said: Has he made the gods one god? Indeed, this is a strange thing. And Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: When God the Almighty sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as a messenger, the Arabs denied that, or those of them denied it, and they said: God is greater than for His Messenger to be a human like Muhammad. So God the Almighty revealed: Is it a wonder to the people? The verse. And his saying: That they will have a sure footing with their Lord, they differed about it. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his saying: And give good tidings to those who believe that they will have a sure footing, meaning that happiness preceded them in the first mention. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: That they will have a sure footing with their Lord, meaning: a good reward for what they have presented. And Ad-Dahhak, Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas, and Abd al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said the same. This is like the saying of God Almighty: To warn of a severe punishment, the verse. And Mujahid said: That they will have a sure footing with their Lord, meaning the righteous deeds are their prayers, their fasting, their charity, and their glorification. He said: And Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, intercedes for them. And so said Zaid bin Aslam and Muqatil bin Hayyan. Qatadah said: A sure footing with their Lord. And Ibn Jarir chose the saying of Mujahid that the righteous deeds that they presented are like what is called a footing in Islam, like the saying of Hassan: We have the upper hand over you and we are behind you in the obedience of God. Follow us. And the saying of Dhu al-Rummah: How many feet do people deny that, with normal calculations, it has flown over the sea? And the Almighty said: The disbelievers said, ‘This is indeed an obvious magician.’ That is, although We sent to them a messenger from among themselves, a man from their own kind, as a bringer of good tidings and a warner, The disbelievers said, ‘This is indeed an obvious magician.’ That is, obvious, and they are the liars in that.

10:3: The Almighty informs us that He is the Lord of the entire world, and that He created the heavens and the earth in six days, it was said like these days, and it was said that each day is like a thousand years of what you count, as will be explained. Then He established the Throne, and the Throne is the greatest of creation and its ceiling. Ibn Abi Hatim said, Hajjaj bin Hamza told us, Abu Usamah told us, Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us, he heard Saad al-Ta'i say: The Throne is a red ruby, and Wahb bin Munabbih said, God created it from His light, and this is strange. And His statement, He directs the affair means He directs the affairs of creation, Not an atom's weight is hidden from Him in the heavens or on the earth, and He is not distracted by one matter from another, nor is He confused by questions, nor is He bored by the importunity of importunate people, nor is He distracted by the management of the great from the small in the mountains and seas, inhabited areas and deserts, And there is no creature on earth but that upon God is its provision the verse. “Not a leaf falls but that He knows it. And there is no grain within the darknesses of the earth and no moist or dry thing but that it is [written] in a clear register.” Al-Darawerdi said on the authority of Sa`d ibn Ishaq ibn Ka`b that he said when this verse was revealed, Indeed, your Lord is God, who created the heavens and the earth, the verse, a large caravan met them and they did not think they were Arabs. They said to them: Who are you? They said: We are from the jinn. We have left the city. This verse has brought us out. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. And His statement: There is no intercessor except after His permission is like the statement of the Most High: Who is he that can intercede with Him except with His permission? And like His statement: And how many an angel is there in the heavens whose intercession will avail nothing except after God gives permission to whom He wills and is pleased with? And His statement: And intercession does not benefit with Him except for him whom He gives permission. And His statement: “That is God, your Lord, so worship Him. Will you not remember?” That is, single Him out in worship alone, with no partner for Him. Will you not remember? That is, you polytheists in your affair worship a god other than Him along with God, and you know that He is the One who is unique in creation, like His statement: And if you ask them who created them, they will surely say, ‘God.’ And His statement: Say, ‘Who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Lord of the Mighty Throne?’ They will say, ‘God.’ Say, ‘Then will you not fear God?’ And so are the verses before and after it.
10:4: The Almighty informs us that the return of creation to Him on the Day of Resurrection will be; He will not leave any of them until He restores them as He began them. Then the Almighty mentioned that just as He began creation, He will restore them. And it is He who begins creation and then repeats it, and that is easier for Him. “That He may reward those who believe and do righteous deeds with justice.” That is, with justice and the fullest recompense. And those who disbelieve will have a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment for what they used to disbelieve. That is, because of their disbelief, they will be tormented on the Day of Resurrection with various types of torment, including poisons, scalding water, and the shade of scalding water. “This, let them taste it: scalding water and pus. And other pairs of its like.” “This is Hell, which the criminals deny. They will circulate between it and scalding water, and there will be a painful torment.”
10:5: The Almighty tells us about the signs He created that indicate the perfection of His power and the greatness of His authority, that He made the ray emanating from the mass of the sun a light and made the ray of the moon a light. This is one art and this is another art, so He differentiated between them so that they would not be confused. He made the power of the sun during the day and the power of the moon during the night, and He determined the phases of the moon. At first it appears small, then its light and mass increase until it becomes full and its fullness is complete. Then it begins to decrease until it returns to its original state in the completion of a month, as the Almighty said: “And the moon - We have determined for it phases until it returns [like] an old dried date stalk. It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day. Each, in an orbit, floats.” And the Almighty said: And the sun and the moon by calculation. And His saying in this noble verse: And He determined for it meaning the moon phases that you may know the number of years and the reckoning. So by the sun the days are known and by the course of the moon the months and years are known. God did not create that except in truth. That is, He did not create it in vain, but He has a great wisdom in that and a conclusive proof. And as the Almighty said: “And We did not create the heaven and the earth and all that is between them in vain. That is the assumption of those who disbelieve. So woe to those who disbelieve from the Fire.” And the Almighty said: “Did you think that We created you in vain and that to Us you would not be returned? So exalted is God, the True King. There is no god but He, Lord of the Noble Throne.” And His statement: We detail the verses means We explain the arguments and evidence for a people who know. And His statement: Indeed, in the alternation of the night and the day means their succession, when one comes, the other goes and when the other goes, the other comes, and it does not delay it at all, as the Almighty said: The night covers the day, pursuing it rapidly. And He said: It is not for the sun to overtake the moon the verse. And the Almighty said: He who splits the dawn and makes the night for rest 3:10, and His saying: And what God has created in the heavens and the earth 3:10, meaning of the signs indicating His greatness, the Almighty, as He said: And how many a sign is there in the heavens and the earth 3:10, and His saying: “Say, ‘Look at what is in the heavens and the earth. But signs and warners do not avail a people who do not believe’” 3:10, and He said: Have they not seen what is before them and what is behind them of the heaven and the earth? 3:10, and He said: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding 3:10, meaning of the intellects. And He said here: Signs for a people who fear God 3:10, meaning of the punishment, wrath, and torment of God.

10:7: God the Almighty says, informing about the state of the wretched ones who disbelieved in meeting God on the Day of Resurrection and do not expect anything in meeting Him, and were satisfied with this worldly life and their souls were reassured by it. Al-Hasan said: By God, they did not adorn it or elevate it until they were satisfied with it, and they are heedless of God's cosmic signs, so they do not contemplate them, and of the religious signs, so they do not obey them. Indeed, their abode on the Day of Resurrection is the Fire, a reward for what they used to earn in their worldly life of sins, transgressions, and crimes, along with what they are in of disbelief in God, His Messenger, and the Last Day.

10:9: This is report about the state of the happy ones who believed in God and believed the messengers and complied with what they were commanded to do and did righteous deeds, that He will guide them through their faith. It is possible that the preposition baa here is causal, so its meaning is that because of their faith in this world, God will guide them on the Day of Resurrection on the straight path until they cross it and are saved to Paradise. It is possible that it is for assistance, as Mujahid said in his statement: Their Lord will guide them through their faith. He said: It will be a light for them by which they walk. Ibn Jurayj said about the verse: His deeds will be presented to him in a beautiful form and a pleasant scent when he rises from his grave, confronting his companion and giving him good report of all that is good, saying to him: Who are you? He will say: I am your work. He will make a light for him before him until he enters Paradise. This is what the Most High said: Their Lord guides them by their faith. As for the disbeliever, his work will appear to him in a bad form and a foul odor, so it will cling to its owner and stick to him until it throws him into the Fire. Something similar was narrated from Qatadah in a mursal form, and God knows best. His statement: “Their call therein will be: ‘Glory be to You, O God.’ And their greeting therein will be: ‘Peace.’ And their final call will be: ‘Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.’” That is, this is the state of the people of Paradise. Ibn Jurayj said: I was informed that His statement: “Their call therein will be: ‘Glory be to You, O God.’” He said: When a bird passes by them desiring it, they will say: Glory be to You, O God. And this is their call. Then the angel will bring them what they desire and greet them, and they will respond to him. This is what He said: “And their greeting therein will be: ‘Peace.’” He said: When they eat, they will praise God. This is what He said: “And their final call will be: ‘Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.’” Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: When the people of Paradise want to supplicate for food, one of them will say, Glory be to You, O God. He said, Then ten thousand servants will stand over one of them, and each servant will have a golden plate containing food that the other does not have. He said, So he will eat from all of them. Sufyan al-Thawri said: When one of them wants to supplicate for something, he will say, Glory be to You, O God. This verse is similar to His statement, “Their greeting on the Day they meet Him will be, ‘Peace.’” And His statement: “They will hear therein no idle talk or sinful speech, but only the word, ‘Peace, peace,’” and His statement: “Peace, a word from a Merciful Lord,” and His statement: “And the angels will enter upon them from every gate, ‘Peace be upon you,’” and the verse, and His statement: And their final call will be, ‘Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds,’ this indicates that He, the Most High, is the One Who is praised forever, the One Who is worshipped throughout all eternity. For this reason, He praised Himself at the beginning of His creation and its continuation, and at the beginning of His Book and at the beginning of His revelation, where He, the Most High, says: Praise be to God, Who has sent down to His servant the Book, “Praise be to God, Who created the heavens and the earth,” and other states that would take too long to list, and that He is the One Who is praised in this world and the next, in this life and in the hereafter, and in all states. For this reason, it is stated in the hadith: The people of Paradise are inspired to glorify and praise as they are inspired to breathe. This is only because they see the increase of God’s blessings upon them, which are repeated and reinstated and increase, and they have no end or duration, for there is no god but Him and no lord but Him.

10:11: The Almighty tells us about His forbearance and kindness to His servants that He does not respond to them if they call upon Him for themselves, their wealth, or their children when they are bored and angry, and that He knows that they do not intend evil to want it, so He does not respond to them in this case out of kindness and mercy, just as He responds to them if they call upon Him for themselves, their wealth, or their children for good, blessing, and growth. That is why He said: And if God were to hasten evil for the people as they hasten good, their term would have been ended for them (al-Baqarah 2:17), meaning if He answered them every time they called upon Him for that, He would have destroyed them. However, this should not be done too much, as came in the hadith narrated by al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar in his Musnad: Muhammad ibn Muammar told us, Yaqub ibn Muhammad told us, Hatim ibn Ismail told us, Yaqub ibn Mujahid Abu Hazrah told us, on the authority of Ubadah ibn al-Walid, Jabir told us, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not call upon yourselves, do not call upon your children, do not call upon your wealth, do not agree with those who… God has an hour in which there is an answer, so He will answer you.” Narrated by Abu Dawud from the hadith of Hatim bin Ismail. Al-Bazzar said: It was narrated by Ubadah bin Al-Walid bin Ubadah bin As-Samit Al-Ansari alone, and no one shared it with him. This is like the saying of God the Almighty: And man invokes evil as he invokes good (al-Ansari 10:10). Mujahid said in his interpretation of this verse: And if God were to hasten for the people evil as they hasten for good (al-Ansari 10:10). It is what a person says to his child or his money when He is angry with him: O God, do not bless him and curse him. If He were to hasten for them an answer in that, they would not be answered in good, it would destroy them.
10:12: The Almighty tells about man and his distress and anxiety if evil befalls him, as He says: And when evil befalls him, he is one of abundant supplication meaning much, and they are in one meaning, because if a hardship befalls him, he is anxious about it and is distressed by it and supplicates a lot at that time, so he supplicates to God to relieve it and lift it from him while he is lying down, sitting, and standing, and in all his states. Then if God relieves his hardship and removes his distress, he turns away and distances himself and goes away as if nothing of that had happened to him. He passed on as if he had not called upon Us for a harm that befell him. Then the Almighty condemned the one who has this description and method, saying: Thus is made attractive to the transgressors what they used to do. As for the one whom God has provided with guidance, success, guidance, and right direction, he is an exception to that, as He says: Except for those who are patient and do righteous deeds. And as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Amazing is the affair of the believer. God does not decree for him a decree except that it is good for him. If a harm befalls him and he is patient, it is good for him, and if it befalls him, If he is happy and grateful, it is better for him, and this is not the case for anyone except the believer.
10:13: God Almighty informed us about what happened to the past generations in their denial of the messengers in what they brought them of clear proofs and arguments, then God made these people successors after them and sent to them a messenger to see their obedience to him and their following of his messenger. In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Saeed, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The world is sweet and green, and God has made you successors in it to see how you act, so beware of the world and beware of women, for the first trial of the Children of Israel was from women. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna told me, Zaid bin Awf Abu Rabi’ah Fahd told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Thabit Al-Banani, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Abi Laila, that Awf bin Malik said to Abu Bakr: I saw in a dream as if a cause was lowered from the sky, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was revived. Then it was repeated and Abu Bakr was revived. Then the people walked around the pulpit, and Umar was three cubits above the pulpit, so Umar said: Leave your vision, we have no interest in it. So when Umar was made successor, he said: O Awf your vision? He said: Do you have any need for my vision or did you not rebuke me? He said: Woe to you, I did not like you to announce the death of the successor of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So he narrated to him the vision until the people reached the pulpit with these three cubits. He said: As for the first of them, he was a successor. As for the second, he does not fear the blame of any critic for God’s sake. As for the three, he is a martyr. He said: So he said: God the Most High says: Then We made you successors on the earth after them to see how you would act. So you have been made successors, O son of Umm Umar, so see how you act. As for his saying: I do not fear the blame of any critic for God’s sake in whatever God wills. As for his saying: A martyr, how can Umar be a martyr while the Muslims are surrounding him?

Then it was repeated and Abu Bakr was revived. Then the people walked around the pulpit, and Umar was three cubits above the pulpit, so Umar said: Leave your vision, we have no interest in it. So when Umar was made successor, he said: O Awf your vision? He said: Do you have any need for my vision or did you not rebuke me? He said: Woe to you, I did not like you to announce the death of the successor of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So he narrated to him the vision until the people reached the pulpit with these three cubits. He said: As for the first of them, he was a successor. As for the second, he does not fear the blame of any critic for God’s sake. As for the three, he is a martyr. He said: So he said: God the Most High says: Then We made you successors on the earth after them to see how you would act. So you have been made successors, O son of Umm Umar, so see how you act. As for his saying: I do not fear the blame of any critic for God’s sake in whatever God wills. As for his saying: A martyr, how can Umar be a martyr while the Muslims are surrounding him?
10:15: God Almighty tells about the stubbornness of the infidels from the polytheists of Quraysh who denied and turned away from it. When the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited to them the Book of God and His clear proof, they said to him: Bring a Qur’an other than this, i.e. reject this and bring us another of a different type or change it to another position. God Almighty said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Say: It is not for me to change it of my own accord.” That is, this is not up to me. Rather, I am a servant who is commanded and a messenger conveying the message of God. “I only follow what is revealed to me. Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a terrible Day.” Then He said, arguing with them about the authenticity of what he brought them: “Say: If God had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you.” That is, I only brought it to you with God’s permission for me to do so, His will and His desire. The proof that I did not invent it from myself nor fabricate it is that you are incapable of opposing it and that you know my truthfulness and honesty since I grew up among you until the time God Almighty sent me. You do not criticize me for anything. They accused me of it, and that is why he said: “I have lived among you a lifetime before this. Do you not understand?” That is, do you not have minds with which to know the truth from falsehood? That is why when Heraclius, the king of Rome, asked Abu Sufyan and those with him about the description of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Heraclius said to Abu Sufyan: Did you accuse him of lying before he said what he said? Abu Sufyan said: I said: No. Abu Sufyan was at that time the leader of the infidels and the chief of the polytheists, and despite this he acknowledged the truth - and the virtue is what the enemies testified to - so Heraclius said to him: Then I know that he would not leave lying to the people and then go and lie about God. Ja’far ibn Abi Talib said to the Negus, the king of Abyssinia: God sent among us a Messenger whose truthfulness, lineage, and trustworthiness we know. The period of his stay among us before the prophethood was forty years, and according to Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, forty-three years, and the correct and well-known is the first.

10:17: God Almighty says, There is no one more unjust, more rebellious, or more criminal than he who invents a lie against God and speaks about God and claims that God sent him, when that was not the case. There is no one who is greater in crime or more unjust than this man. The matter of such a person is not hidden from the foolish, so how can the state of this person be confused with the prophets? If someone says this statement, whether truthfully or lying, God must set up evidence against him of his righteousness or immorality that is clearer than the sun. The difference between Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Musaylimah the Liar is clearer to whoever sees them than the difference between the time of the forenoon and the middle of the night in the darkest of nights. From the characteristics, actions, and speech of each of them, whoever has insight can infer the truthfulness of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the lies of Musaylimah the Liar, Sajah, and Al-Aswad Al-Ansi. Abdullah bin Salam said: When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to Medina, the people were startled and I was among those who were startled. When I saw him, I knew that his face was not the face of a lying man. He said: The first thing I heard him say was: “O people, spread peace, feed the poor, maintain family ties, and pray at night while people are asleep, and you will enter Paradise in peace.” When the delegation of Dhimam bin Tha’labah came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) with his people, Banu Sa’d bin Bakr, he said to the Messenger of God, among other things, Who raised this sky? He said: God. He said: And who erected these mountains? He said: God. He said: And who flattened this earth? He said: God. He said: Then by the One Who raised the sky, erected these mountains, and flattened this earth, has God sent you to all people? He said: O God, yes. Then he asked him about prayer, zakat, Hajj, and fasting, and he would swear this oath for each one, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would swear to him. He said to him: You have spoken the truth, and by He who sent you with the truth, I will neither add to that nor subtract from that. So this man was satisfied with just this, and he was certain of his truthfulness, may God bless him and grant him peace, because of what he saw and witnessed of the evidence indicating it. Hassan bin Thabit said: If there were no clear verses in it, its intuition would have brought you the report. As for Musaylima, whoever of those with insight saw him would inevitably know his affair with his weak, not eloquent, and his actions which were not good, but rather ugly, and his Qur’an which will make him eternal in Hell on the Day of Regret and Disgrace. How many differences there are between the words of God Almighty: “God - there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep,” etc. And the words of Musaylima, may God curse and make ugly: O frog, daughter of two frogs, purify yourself as you purify, neither cloud the water nor prevent the drinker. And his words, may God curse him: God has bestowed favor upon the pregnant woman, for He has brought forth from her a soul that runs, from between the peritoneum and the viscera. And his words, may God make him eternal in the fire of Hell. And he did: The elephant, and what do you know about the elephant? It has a long trunk. And his saying, may God distance him from His mercy: And the kneaders kneading, and the bakers baking bread, and the morsels morsels, ghee and lard. Indeed, the Quraysh are a people who transgress. And other superstitions and deliriums that children are loath to utter except in mockery and ridicule. For this reason, God crushed his nose, and he drank his death on the day of the Garden of Death, and his family was torn apart. And his companions and his family cursed him. They came to Abu Bakr repentant, and they came to the religion of God, desirous. Abu Bakr, the successor of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked them to recite to him something from the Quran of Musaylima, may God curse him. They asked him to exempt them from that, but he refused, unless they read something from it so that those of the people who had not heard it could hear it, and they would know the superiority of what they were upon of guidance and knowledge. So they read to him some of what we have mentioned and similar things. When they finished, Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said to them: Woe to you, where did your minds go? By God, this did not come from God. They mentioned that Amr ibn al-Aas came to Musaylima and he was a friend of his in the pre-Islamic era. Amr had not yet converted to Islam, so Musaylima said to him: Woe to you, Amr. What was revealed to your companion, meaning the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, during this period? He said: I heard his companions reciting a great short surah. He said: What is it? He said: “By the declining day. Indeed, mankind is in loss” to the end of the surah. Musaylima thought for a moment and then said: What has been revealed to me like it? He said: What is it? He said: O wool, O wool, you are nothing but two ears and a chest, and the rest of you is a hole and a pit. What do you think, O Amr? Amr said to him: By God, you know that I know that you are lying. If this was from a polytheist in his state of polytheism, he did not doubt the state of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his truthfulness, and the state of Musaylimah may God curse him and his denial, then how about those with insight and understanding, and those with sound, upright minds and wisdom? For this reason, God the Almighty said: “And who is more unjust than he who invents a lie about God or says, ‘It has been revealed to me,’ while nothing has been revealed to him? And he who says, ‘I will reveal the like of what God has revealed,’” and He said in this noble verse: And who is more unjust than he who invents a lie about God or denies His signs? Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed. And likewise, whoever denies the truth that the messengers brought and the proofs are established against him, no one is more unjust than him, as it came in the hadith: The most rebellious of people against God is a man who killed a prophet or was killed by a prophet.
10:18: God Almighty denounces the polytheists who worshipped other gods with God, thinking that their intercession with God would benefit them. God Almighty informed us that they neither harm nor benefit nor possess anything, and nothing of what they claim about them will happen and will never happen. For this reason God Almighty said: “Say: Do you inform God of what He does not know in the heavens or on the earth?” Ibn Jarir said: Its meaning is: Do you inform God of what is not in the heavens or on the earth? Then He exalted Himself above their polytheism and disbelief, saying: Glory be to Him, and He is exalted above what they associate with Him. Then the Most High informed us that this polytheism is a new phenomenon among people, occurring after it did not exist, and that all people were of one religion, which is Islam. Ibn Abbas said: There were ten centuries between Adam and Noah, all of them of Islam, then differences arose among people and idols, rivals, and statues were worshipped, so God sent the messengers with His signs, His proofs, His conclusive arguments, and His overwhelming proofs, so that whoever is to perish will perish by clear evidence, and whoever lives will live by clear evidence. And His statement: And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, the verse, meaning had it not been for what preceded from God Almighty that He would not punish anyone except after the proof was established against him, and that He had given creation a set term, He would have judged between them regarding what they differed over, so He made the believers happy and helped the disbelievers.

10:20: That is, these stubborn, lying disbelievers say: Why was a sign not sent down to Muhammad from his Lord? They mean as God gave the she-camel to Thamud, or that He should turn Safa into gold for them, or remove the mountains of Mecca from them and replace it with gardens and rivers, or something similar to what God is capable of, but He is wise in His actions and words, as God Almighty said: “Blessed be He who, if He wills, can grant you better than that - gardens beneath which rivers flow, and can grant you palaces. * Rather, they have denied the Hour, and We have prepared for whoever denies the Hour a Blaze.” And as He said: And nothing prevented Us from sending signs except that the former peoples denied them. The verse, God Almighty says: Indeed, My way with My creation is that when I give them what they ask for, if they believe, otherwise I hasten the punishment upon them. That is why when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was given the choice between giving them what they asked for, if they believed, otherwise they would be punished, and giving them respite, he chose to give them respite, as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was patient with them more than once. That is why God Almighty said, guiding His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the answer to what they asked: Say, ‘The unseen is only for God,’ meaning that the entire matter belongs to God, and He knows the consequences of matters. Then wait, for I am with you among those who wait. That is, if you do not believe until you see what you asked for, then wait for God’s judgment regarding me and you. This is despite the fact that they had seen greater signs from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, than what they asked for when he pointed in their presence to the moon on the night of its fullness, and it split into two, one group behind the mountain and the other group in front of it. This is greater than all the earthly signs that they asked for and what they did not ask for. If God had known that they asked for that for guidance and confirmation, He would have answered them. However, He knew that they were only asking out of stubbornness and obstinacy, so He left them in what troubled them, and He knew that none of them would believe, as God the Most High said: Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe, even if every sign came to them. And the Almighty said: And if We sent down to them angels and the dead spoke to them and We gathered together all things before them, they would not believe unless God willed verse, and because of their stubbornness, as in the Almighty’s saying: And if We opened to them a gate from the heaven verse, and the Almighty’s saying: And if they saw a fragment of the sky falling verse, and the Almighty said: And if We sent down to you a book on paper and they touched it with their hands, those who disbelieved would say, ‘This is not but obvious magic’ verse. Such people are less than those who are answered to what they asked for, because there is no benefit in answering them, as it revolves around their stubbornness and obstinacy due to their great wickedness and corruption. For this reason, He said: So wait, for I am with you among those who wait.
10:21: God Almighty tells us that if He lets people taste mercy after a hardship that has befallen them, such as ease after hardship, fertility after drought, rain after famine, and the like, Then they have a plan concerning Our signs. Mujahid said: It is mockery and denial, like His statement: And when harm touches man, he invokes Us, lying on his side, or sitting, or standing, the verse. And in the Sahih, it is reported that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed the dawn prayer with them after a rain fell during the night, then he said: Do you know what your Lord said last night? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: “He said: There have arisen among My servants some who believe in Me and some who disbelieve. As for he who says, ‘We have rain by the grace and mercy of God,’ he is a believer in Me and a disbeliever in the star. As for he who says, ‘We have rain by the force of such and such a star,’ he is a disbeliever in Me and a believer in the star.” And His statement: Say, ‘God is swifter in plotting,’ means more rapid in enticing and giving respite, until the one who thinks among the criminals thinks that he is not being punished and is only being given a respite. Then he is taken by surprise, and the noble scribes write down for him everything he does and count it against him, then they present it to the Knower of the Unseen and the Seen, and He will reward him for the great and the small, the speck and the small amount. Then the Almighty informed us that it is He who guides you on land and sea meaning He protects you and guards you with His protection until, when you are in the ships and they sail with them with a fair wind and they rejoice in it meaning in the speed of their journey together, then while they are like that, there comes to it meaning those ships a violent wind meaning strong and the waves come upon them from every side meaning the sea lashes them and they think that they are surrounded meaning they are destroyed call upon God, sincerely devoting their religion to Him meaning they do not call upon any idol or statue with Him, but rather they single Him out in supplication and entreaty, as the Almighty said: “And when harm touches you at sea, those you call upon are lost except Him. But when He delivers you to land, you turn away, and man is ever ungrateful” and He said here: Call upon God, sincerely devoting His religion, ‘If You should save us from this’ meaning this state, “we will surely be among the grateful’ meaning we will not associate anyone with You and we will single You out in worship there as We singled You out in supplication here. God the Almighty said: So when He has saved them meaning from that The predicament If they are to transgress upon the earth without right meaning as if none of that had happened as if he had not called upon Us to a harm that had befallen him. Then the Almighty said: O mankind, your transgression is only against yourselves meaning that you will only taste the consequences of this transgression and you will not harm anyone else with it, as came in the hadith There is no sin more deserving of God hastening its punishment in this world along with what God has in store for its perpetrator in the Hereafter than transgression and severing family ties. And His saying: The enjoyment of worldly life meaning that you will only have enjoyment in this lowly and insignificant worldly life Then to Us is your return meaning your destiny and your final destination Then We will inform you meaning We will tell you of all your deeds and repay you for them, so whoever finds good, let him praise God, and whoever finds otherwise, let him blame no one but himself.

10:24: The Blessed and Most High gave an example of the flower of this worldly life and its adornment and how quickly it passes and vanishes, with the plants that God brought forth from the earth, with water sent down from the sky, from what people eat of crops and fruits of different types and kinds, and what livestock eat of stubble and reeds and other things, until the earth takes on its adornment meaning its perishable adornment and is beautified meaning it is made beautiful by what comes out of its highlands of fresh flowers of different shapes and colors and its people who planted and cultivated it think that they have power over it meaning over its pruning and harvesting, but while they are like that, a thunderbolt or a strong, cold wind comes upon it, drying up its leaves and destroying its fruits. For this reason, the Most High said: Our command came to it by night or by day, and We made it a harvest meaning dry after its greenness and freshness as if it had never flourished yesterday meaning as if it had never been beautiful before that. Qatada said: As if you had never been rich, as if you had never enjoyed anything. And so it is with matters after their disappearance, as if they had never existed. And for this reason it is stated in the hadith: “The most affluent of the people of this world will be brought and dipped in the Fire once, and it will be said to him, ‘Have you ever seen any good? Have you ever experienced any pleasure?’ He will say, ‘No.’ And the most severely punished of the people of this world will be brought and dipped in pleasure once, and it will be said to him, ‘Have you ever seen any misery?’ He will say, ‘No.’” And God the Almighty said, informing about those who are destroyed: So they will be in their homes, prostrate, as if they had never prospered therein. Then God the Almighty said: Thus do We explain the signs, meaning, We explain the arguments and evidence for a people who reflect, so they will consider this example of the world’s rapid disappearance from its people, despite their being deceived by it, and their being able to trust and trust in its promises and its slipping away from them, for it is its nature to flee from those who seek it, and to seek those who flee from it. God the Almighty has given an example of the world with the plants of the earth in more than one verse in His Noble Book, as He said in Surat al-Kahf 18:“And present to them the example of the life of this world: it is like water which We send down from the sky, and the plants of the earth mingle with it, and it becomes dry stubble, scattered by the winds. And God is over all things.” Powerful and so in Surat Az-Zumar and Surat Al-Hadid, God gives an example of the life of this world. 10:45: God Almighty says, reminding people of the coming of the Hour and their gathering from their graves to the places of al-Qiyamah 75:And the Day He will gather them verse. And as He said: On the Day they see what they are promised, it will be as if they had not remained except an hour of a day. And as He said: On the Day they see it, it will be as if they had not remained except an afternoon or a morning thereof. And the Most High said: “On the Day the Trumpet is blown and We gather the criminals that Day blue-eyed, whispering to one another, ‘You remained only ten.’ We know best what they say when the best of them in conduct says, ‘You remained only a day.’” And the Most High said: And on the Day the Hour will appear, the criminals will swear that they had not remained except an hour. And the two verses, and all of this is evidence of the brevity of worldly life in the Hereafter, as He said: “He will say, ‘How many years have you remained on the earth?’ They will say, ‘We remained a day or part of a day. So ask the counters.’ He will say, ‘You remained only a little, if you only knew.’” And His saying: They will recognize one another, meaning that children will recognize fathers and relatives as they were in this world, but each will be preoccupied with himself. So when the Trumpet is blown, there will be no kinship between them. And the Most High said: And no intimate friend will ask an intimate friend. And the two verses, and His saying: He has certainly lost. Those who denied the meeting with God and were not guided. As God Almighty said: Woe, that Day, to the deniers. Because they will lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Is that not the clear loss? There is no greater loss than the loss of someone who is separated from his loved ones on the Day of Regret and Remorse.
10:46: God the Almighty says, addressing His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace: And if We show you some of what We promise them, meaning We take revenge on them during your lifetime so that your eyes may be comforted by them, or We cause you to die, then to Us is their return, meaning their destiny and their final destination, and God is Witness to their actions after you. At-Tabarani said: Abdullah bin Ahmad told us, Uqbah bin Makram told us, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, Dawud bin al-Jarud told us, on the authority of Abu al-Salil, on the authority of Hudhayfah bin Asid, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: My nation was presented to me last night in this room, its beginning and its end. A man said: O Messenger of God, were those who were created presented to you, so how about those who were not created? He said: They were made for me in clay, so that I could recognize one of them as one of you is his companion. It was narrated by Muhammad bin Uthman bin Abi Shaybah, on the authority of Uqbah bin Makram, on the authority of Yunus bin Bakir, on the authority of Ziyad bin al-Mundhir, on the authority of Abu al-Tufayl, on the authority of Hudhayfah bin Asid, with a similar wording. And His statement: And for every nation is a messenger, so when their messenger comes, Mujahid said: meaning on the Day of Resurrection, it will be judged between them in justice, the verse, like the statement of God Almighty: And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, the verse, so every nation will be presented to God in the presence of its messenger and the book of its deeds, good and evil, will be placed as a witness against them and their guardian angels will also be witnesses, nation after nation. And this noble nation, even though it was the last of the nations in creation, will be the first of the nations on the Day of Resurrection to be judged between them and judged for them, as came in the two Sahihs on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: We are the last, the foremost on the Day of Resurrection, the judge will judge for them before the creation. So his nation only won the race because of the honor of its messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, forever until the Day of Judgment.

10:48: God Almighty says, informing about the disbelief of these polytheists in their hastening of the punishment and their asking about its time before it is appointed, which is of no benefit to them, as He says: Those who do not believe in it hasten it, but those who believe are fearful of it and know that it is the truth, meaning that it will inevitably happen and will occur, even if they do not know its exact time. For this reason, God Almighty guided His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to answer them, saying: Say, ‘I do not control for myself any harm or benefit,’ the verse, meaning that I do not say anything except what He has taught me, and I am not able to do anything that He has kept to Himself unless God informs me of it, for I am His servant and Messenger to you, and I have informed you of the coming of the Hour and that it will happen, but He has not informed me of its time, but for every nation there is a term, meaning for every century there is a specified period of life, so when their term has expired, they will not delay it an hour, nor will they advance it, as He says: And God will not delay a soul when its term has come, the verse. Then He informed that God’s punishment will come to them suddenly, saying: Say, ‘Have you considered, if God wills, then He wills. Has His punishment come upon you by night or by day? That is, by night or by day. What are the criminals hastening for? Then, when it comes, will you believe in it now, while you used to hasten it? That is, when the punishment comes to them, they will say, Our Lord, we have seen and heard. The verse. And God Almighty said: “But when they saw Our punishment, they said, ‘We believe in God alone and disbelieve in that which we used to associate with Him.’ But their belief did not benefit them when they saw Our punishment. This is the way of God which has already been with His servants. And there the disbelievers lost out.” Then it will be said to those who did wrong, ‘Taste the punishment of eternity.’ That is, on the Day of Resurrection, this will be said to them as a rebuke and a rebuke, like His statement: “The Day they are summoned to the fire of Hell. It will be summoned. This is the fire which you used to deny. Is this magic, or do you not see? Enter it, so be patient or do not be patient. It is all the same to you. You will only be recompensed for what you used to do.”

10:53: God Almighty says: And they ask you, Is it true? meaning the Resurrection and the Resurrection from the graves after the bodies have become dust. "Say, 'Yes, by my Lord, it is the truth. And you cannot escape.'" meaning that your becoming dust is not a stumbling block for God to restore you as He began you from nothingness. His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, 'Be,' and it is. This verse has no parallel in the Qur'an except for two other verses in which God Almighty commands His Messenger to swear by it against those who deny the Resurrection in Surat Saba': And those who disbelieve say, 'The Hour will not come to us.' Say, 'Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you.' And in al-Taghabun 64:"Those who disbelieve claim that they will not be resurrected. Say, 'Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected. Then you will surely be informed of what you did.' And that is easy for God." Then God Almighty informs that when the Resurrection comes, the disbeliever will wish that he could ransom himself from God's punishment by filling the earth with gold. And they will conceal their regret when they see the punishment, and it will be judged between them with justice, meaning with truth, and they will not be wronged.

10:57: The Almighty says, thanking His creation for what He sent down from the Great Qur’an to His noble Messenger: O mankind, there has come to you instruction from your Lord meaning a deterrent from indecencies and a healing for what is in the breasts meaning from doubts and suspicions, which is the removal of what is in them of filth and impurity, and guidance and mercy, meaning that guidance and mercy from God the Almighty are obtained through it, and that is only for those who believe in it and believe in what is in it, like His Almighty saying: And We send down from the Qur’an that which is healing and mercy for the believers, but it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss and His saying: Say, ‘It is for those who believe, guidance and healing’ and the verse, and His Almighty saying: Say, ‘In the bounty of God and in His mercy, so in that let them rejoice’ meaning in what came to them from God of guidance and the religion of truth, so let them rejoice, for it is the most appropriate thing for them to rejoice in. The verse, and he mentioned with his chain of transmission on the authority of Baqiyah bin Al-Walid on the authority of Safwan bin Amr, I heard Aifa bin Abdul Kila’i say: When the tax of Iraq was presented to Umar, may God be pleased with him, Umar and his freedman went out and Umar began to count the camels and they were more than that, so Umar began to say, Praise be to God Almighty, and his freedman said, By God, this is from the grace and mercy of God. So Umar said, “You have lied, this is not what God Almighty says: ‘Say, “By the grace of God and by His mercy,”’ the verse, and this is what they agree upon. Al-Hafiz Abu Al-Qasim Al-Tabarani has transmitted it, so he narrated it on the authority of Abu Zur’ah Al-Dimashqi on the authority of Haywah bin Shuraih on the authority of Baqiyah, and he mentioned it.

10:59: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, Abdur-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam and others said: It was revealed as a denunciation of the polytheists regarding what they permitted and prohibited of the Baha'ir, Sawa'ib and Wasa'il, like the Almighty's saying: "And they assigned to God a share of what He created of crops and livestock" (Al-An'am 14:10). Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad bin Ja'far told us, Shu'bah told us on the authority of Abu Ishaq, I heard Abu Al-Ahwas, who is Awf bin Malik bin Nadlah, narrating on the authority of his father who said: I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I was in a shabby state. He said: "Do you have any money?" I said: "Yes." He said: "From what money?" He said: "From all money, from camels, slaves, horses and sheep." He said: "If God gives you money, let it be seen on you." He said: "Do your camels give birth with their ears intact, and you go to a razor and cut off their ears and say: This is a Baha'ir, and tear their skins and say: This is a Sram and forbid them to yourself and your family? He said: Yes. He said: Then what God has given you is permissible for you. God is stronger than your helper, and Moses, God is stronger than your helper.” And he mentioned the rest of the hadith. Then he narrated it on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah on the authority of Abu al-Zahra’ Amr ibn Amr on the authority of his uncle Abu al-Ahwas, and on the authority of Bahz ibn Asad on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah on the authority of Abdul Malik ibn Umair on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas with it. This is a good hadith with a strong chain of transmission. God the Almighty has denounced those who forbade what God has permitted or permitted what He has forbidden merely on the basis of opinions and whims that have no basis or evidence for them. Then He threatened them for that on the Day of Resurrection, saying: And what do those who invent lies about God think on the Day of Resurrection? That is, what do they think He will do to them on the Day of Resurrection? And His statement: Indeed, God is full of bounty to mankind, Ibn Jarir said: In His not hastening their punishment in this world I said and it is possible that what is meant is that He is full of bounty to mankind in what He has permitted for them from what He has created of benefits in this world and He has not forbidden them except what is harmful to them in their world or religion. But most of them are not grateful, rather they forbid what God has bestowed upon them, and they make things difficult for themselves, making some permissible and some… Forbidden. This is what the polytheists have fallen into in what they have legislated for themselves, and the People of the Book have fallen into in what they have innovated in their religion. Ibn Abi Hatim said in his interpretation of this verse: My father told us, Ahmad ibn Abi al-Hawari told us, Rabah told us, Abdullah ibn Sulayman told us, Musa ibn al-Sabah told us, regarding the words of God Almighty: Indeed, God is full of bounty to mankind, he said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, the people of God Almighty’s guardianship will be brought and they will stand before God Almighty in three categories. He said: A man from the first category will be brought and He will say: My servant, what did you do? He will say: O Lord, You created Paradise, its trees, its fruits, its rivers, its houris, its delights, and what You have prepared for the people of Your obedience therein. So I stayed up all night and thirsted all day out of longing for it. He said: God the Almighty will say: My servant, you only worked this Paradise for Paradise, so enter it. And out of My favor to you, I have freed you from the Fire. And out of My favor to you, I am admitting you to My Paradise. So he and those with him will enter Paradise. He said: Then a man from the second category will be brought and My servant will say: Why did you work this? He will say: O Lord, You created a Fire and created its shackles, its blazing heat, its poisonous winds, and what You have prepared for Your enemies and those who disobey You in it. So I stayed up all night and was thirsty during the day out of fear of it. So My servant will say: I only did that out of fear of My Fire. So I have freed you from the Fire. And out of My favor to you, I am admitting you to My Paradise. So he and those with him will enter Paradise. Then a man from the third category will be brought and My servant will say: Why did you work this? He will say: O Lord, out of love for You and longing for You, and by Your might, I stayed up all night and was thirsty during the day out of longing for You and love for You. Then the Blessed and Exalted says: My servant, you only did this out of love for Me and longing for Me. Then the Lord, may He be glorified and exalted, appears to him and says: Here I am, so look at Me. Then He says: It is from My favor upon you that I free you from the Fire, allow you into My Paradise, have My angels visit you, and greet you with My own peace. Then he and those with him enter Paradise.

10:61: The Almighty informs His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that He knows all his conditions and the conditions of his nation and all creation at every hour, moment and instant, and that nothing escapes His knowledge and sight, in the heavens or on the earth, nor anything smaller or larger than it, except in a clear book, as He says: “And with Him are the keys of the unseen, none knows them but He. And He knows what is on the land and the sea. Not a leaf falls but that He knows it. And there is no grain within the darknesses of the earth and no moist or dry thing but that it is in a clear book.” So the Almighty informed that He knows the movement of trees and other inanimate objects, as well as the wandering animals, in His statement: And there is no creature on earth or bird that flies with its wings except that they are communities like you 3:10. And the Almighty said: And there is no creature on earth but that upon God is its provision 3:10. If this is His knowledge of the movements of these things, then how is His knowledge of the movements of those who are charged with worship, as the Almighty said: “And put your trust in the Almighty, the Merciful * Who sees you when you stand * And your turning over in Prostrators. That is why God Almighty said: “And you are not engaged in any affair, nor do you recite from it any Qur’an, nor do you do any deed, but We are witnesses over you when you are engaged in it.” That is, when you undertake that thing, We are watching you, seeing you, and hearing you. That is why the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said when Gabriel asked him about ihsan, That you worship God as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then He sees you.
10:62: God Almighty tells us that His friends are those who believed and were pious, as their Lord explained, so everyone who was pious was a friend of God, so there is no fear upon them, meaning in what they will face of the terrors of the Hereafter, nor will they grieve, for what is behind them in this world. Abdullah bin Masoud, Ibn Abbas, and more than one of the early Muslims said that God’s friends are those who, when they are seen, God is remembered. This was mentioned in a hadith with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, as Al-Bazzar said: Ali bin Harb Al-Razi told us, Muhammad bin Saeed bin Sabeq told us, Yaqub bin Abdullah Al-Ash’ari, who is Al-Qummi, told us, on the authority of Ja’far bin Abi Al-Mughira, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A man said: O Messenger of God, who are God’s friends? He said, Those who, when they are seen, remember God. Then Al-Bazzar said, It was narrated on the authority of Saeed, without a chain of transmission. Ibn Jarir said, “Abu Hisham Al-Rifai told us, Abu Fadil told us, Abu Amara bin Al-Qa’qa’ told us, on the authority of Abu Zur’ah, on the authority of Amr bin Jarir Al-Bajali, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “Among the servants of God are servants whom the prophets and martyrs envy.” It was said, Who are they, O Messenger of God, so that we may love them? He said: “They are people who love one another for the sake of God without wealth or lineage, their faces are light upon pulpits of light, they do not fear when people fear, nor do they grieve when people grieve.” Then he recited: Behold, for the friends of God there is no fear concerning them, nor shall they grieve. Then Abu Dawud also narrated it from the hadith of Jarir, from Ammarah ibn al-Qa’qa’, from Abu Zur’ah, from Amr ibn Jarir, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a similar manner. This is also a good chain of transmission, except that it is interrupted between Abu Zur’ah and Umar ibn al-Khattab, and God knows best. In the hadith of Imam Ahmad, from Abu al-Nadr, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanim, from Abu Malik al-Ash’ari, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There will come from the midst of the people and the tribes, people who are not connected by close kinship ties, who love one another for the sake of God and are united for the sake of God. On the Day of Resurrection, God will place for them pulpits of light and seat them on them, people will be terrified but they will not be terrified. They are the friends of God, who have no fear, nor will they grieve.” The hadith is lengthy. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Dhakwan Abu Salih, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Abu al-Darda’, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding His statement: For them is good tidings in the life of this world and in the Hereafter, he said: A righteous vision that a Muslim sees or is seen for him. Ibn Jarir said: Abu al-Sa’ib told me, Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Yasar, on the authority of a man from the people of Egypt, on the authority of Abu al-Darda’, regarding His statement: For them is good tidings in the life of this world and in the Hereafter, he said: A man asked Abu al-Darda’ about this verse, and he said: You have asked about something that I have not heard anyone ask about after a man asked about it, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: It is a righteous vision that a Muslim sees or is seen for him, which is good tidings in the life of this world and its good tidings in the Hereafter are Paradise. Then Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn al-Munkadir, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Yasar, on the authority of a man from the people of Egypt, that he asked Abu al-Darda’ about this verse, and he mentioned something similar to what was mentioned above. Then Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna told me, Hajjaj ibn Munhal told us, he told us: Hammad bin Zaid, on the authority of Asim bin Bahdalah, on the authority of Abu Salih, said: I heard Abu Darda’ being asked about this verse: Those who believe and fear God, for them are good tidings. He mentioned something similar to it. Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Aban told us, Yahya told us, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Ubadah bin al-Samit, that he asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, what do you think of the statement of God, the Most High: For them are good tidings in the life of this world and in the Hereafter? He said: “You have asked me about something that no one from my nation has asked me about, or no one before you has said anything about it - that is the righteous vision that a man sees or that is seen for him.” And Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated it likewise on the authority of Imran al-Qattan on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, and al-Awza’i narrated it on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, and he mentioned it. And Ali bin al-Mubarak narrated it on the authority of Yahya on the authority of Abu Salamah, who said: Tell us on the authority of Ubadah bin al-Samit, who asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about this verse, and he mentioned it. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Hamid al-Himsi told me, Yahya ibn Saeed told us, Umar ibn Amr ibn Abd al-Ahmoosi told us, on the authority of Hamid ibn Abdullah al-Muzani, who said: A man came to Ubadah ibn al-Samit and said: There is a verse in the Book of God that I should ask you about. God the Most High said: For them is good tidings in the life of this world. Ubadah said: No one has asked me about it before you. I asked the Prophet of God about it and he said something similar: “No one has asked me about it before you: the righteous vision that a believing servant sees in his sleep or that is seen for him.” Then he narrated it from the hadith of Musa ibn Ubaydah on the authority of Ayoub ibn Khalid ibn Safwan on the authority of Ubadah ibn al-Samit that he said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: For them is good tidings in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. We have learned about the good tidings of the Hereafter, Paradise, so what is the good tidings of this world? He said: “A righteous vision is seen by a servant or is seen for him. It is one of forty-four or seventy parts of prophecy.” Imam Ahmad also said: Buhaiz told us, Hammad told us, Abu Imran told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin As-Samit, on the authority of Abu Dharr, that he said: O Messenger of God, a man does a deed and people praise him for it and commend him for it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: That is the immediate good report for the believer. Narrated by Muslim. Ahmad also said: Hasan, meaning As-Ashib, told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Diraj told us, on the authority of Abdur-Rahman bin Jubayr, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: They will have good report of this world and in the Hereafter. He said: A righteous vision that a believer is given good report of is one of forty-nine parts of prophecy. So whoever sees that, let him tell of it. And whoever sees anything other than that, it is from Satan to make him sad. So let him spit to his left three times and say Allahu Akbar and not tell anyone about it. They did not narrate it. Ibn Jarir said: Yunus told me, Ibn Wahb told us, Amr ibn al-Harith told us, Diraj Abu al-Samh told him, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “They will have good tidings in this worldly life. A righteous vision that a believer is given good tidings of is one of forty-six parts of prophecy.” Ibn Jarir also said: Muhammad ibn Abi Hatim al-Mu’addib told us, Ammar ibn Muhammad told us, al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: They will have good tidings in this worldly life and in the Hereafter. He said: In this world, a righteous vision that a servant sees or that is seen for him, and in the Hereafter, it is Paradise. Then he narrated it on the authority of Abu Kurayb, on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that he said: A good vision is good tidings from God, and it is one of the good tidings. This is how he narrated it from this chain of transmission, without a chain of transmission. He also said: Abu Kurayb told us, Abu Bakr told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God’s prayers and peace be upon him: A good vision is a good omen that a Muslim sees or that is seen for him. Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad bin Hammad al-Dulabi told me, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ubayd God bin Abi Yazid, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Saba’ bin Thabit, on the authority of Umm Kuraiz al-Ka’biyyah, I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Prophethood has gone, but the good tidings remain. And thus it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, Abu Hurayrah, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Urwah bin al-Zubayr, Yahya bin Abi Katheer, Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, Ata’ bin Abi Rabah, and others that they interpreted this as a good dream. It was said: What is meant by this is the good report of the angels to the believer when he is dying of Paradise and forgiveness, as God Almighty said: “Indeed, those who say, ‘Our Lord is God,’ and then remain on a right course - the angels will descend upon them, [saying], ‘Do not fear and do not grieve but receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised. We are your allies in worldly life and in the Hereafter. And you will have therein whatever your souls desire, and you will have therein whatever you request - an accommodation from a Forgiving, Merciful.’” And in the hadith of Al-Baraa’, may God be pleased with him, that when death approaches the believer, angels with white faces and white clothes come to him and say, Come out, O good soul, to a spirit of freshness and fragrance and a Lord who is not angry. So it comes out of his mouth as a drop flows from the mouth of a water-skinner. As for their good report of the Hereafter, it is as God Almighty said: The greatest terror will not grieve them, and the angels will meet them, [saying], ‘This is your Day which you were promised.’ And God Almighty said: “The Day you see the believing men and believing women, their light proceeding before them and on their right, [saying], ‘Your good tidings this Day are Gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein you will abide eternally. That is what is the great attainment.’” And His statement: There is no changing the words of God Almighty. God” meaning this promise cannot be changed, broken or altered, but rather it is established, confirmed and inevitable. That is the great success.

10:65: God Almighty says to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace: "And let not the words of these polytheists grieve you. Seek God's help against them and put your trust in Him, for all glory belongs to God, that is, all of it belongs to Him, to His Messenger, and to the believers. "He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing." That is, the All-Hearing of the words of His servants, the All-Knowing of their conditions. Then God Almighty informed us that He owns the heavens and the earth, and that the polytheists worship idols that do not possess anything, neither harm nor benefit, and they have no evidence for their worship of them. Rather, they only follow their conjectures, their guesses, their lies, and their slander. Then He informed us that He is the One who made the night for His servants to rest in, that is, to rest from their fatigue, their fatigue, and their movements. "And the day to see," that is, to illuminate their livelihood, their efforts, their travels, and their interests. "Indeed in that are signs for a people who listen," that is, they hear these arguments and evidence, so they consider them and infer the greatness of their Creator, their Destiner, and their course.

10:68: The Almighty says, denying those who claim that He has a son: Glory be to Him! He is the Rich. That is, He is sanctified from that. He is the Rich from everything other than Him, and everything is in need of Him. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. That is, how can He have a son from what He created, and everything that belongs to Him is His servant? You have no authority for this. That is, you do not have evidence for what you say of lies and slander. Do you say about God what you do not know? A denial, a definite threat, and a severe intimidation, as the Almighty says: “And they say, ‘The Most Gracious has taken a son.’ You have certainly come up with a thing outrageous. The heavens almost burst from it, and the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse in devastation. That they attribute to the Most Gracious a son. It is not befitting for the Most Gracious to take a son. There is none in the heavens and the earth but comes to the Most Gracious as a servant. He has already enumerated them and counted them one by one. And all of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone.” Then the Almighty threatens those who lie against Him and slander those who claim that He has a son, that they will not succeed in this world or in the Hereafter. As for this world, if He tempts them and gives them respite, He will give them enjoyment for a little while. Then We will force them to a severe punishment, as God Almighty said here: Enjoyment in this world, meaning a short period. Then to Us is their return, meaning the Day of Resurrection. Then We will make them taste the severe punishment, meaning the painful, agonizing one. Because they used to disbelieve, meaning because of their disbelief, fabrications, and lies against God in what they claimed of slander and falsehood.

10:79: God the Almighty mentioned the story of the magicians with Moses, peace be upon him, in Surat Al-A'raf, and we have already discussed it there, in this Surah, in Surat Taha, and in Ash-Shu'ara'. This is because Pharaoh, may God curse him, wanted to fool around with the people and oppose what Moses, peace be upon him, brought of the clear truth, with the trappings of magicians and sorcerers. They said, 'We believe in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Moses and Aaron.'" You should recite in a vessel containing water, then pour the verse from Surat Yunus on the head of the bewitched person: “So when they cast, Moses said, ‘What you have brought is magic. Indeed, God will invalidate it. Indeed, God does not amend the work of corrupters. And God will establish the truth with His words, even though the criminals dislike it. ’” And the other verse: So the truth occurred, and what they were doing was invalidated. To the end of the four verses, and His saying: They have only made a magician's trick, and the magician will not succeed wherever he goes.

Indeed, God will invalidate it. Indeed, God does not amend the work of corrupters. And God will establish the truth with His words, even though the criminals dislike it. ’” And the other verse: So the truth occurred, and what they were doing was invalidated. 10:82: God the Almighty mentioned the story of the magicians with Moses, peace be upon him, in Surat Al-A'raf, and we have already discussed it there, in this Surah, in Surat Taha, and in Ash-Shu'ara'. This is because Pharaoh, may God curse him, wanted to fool around with the people and oppose what Moses, peace be upon him, brought of the clear truth, with the trappings of magicians and sorcerers. The system was reversed and he did not achieve his goal. The divine proofs appeared in that general gathering: "And the magicians fell down in prostration. They said, 'We believe in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Moses and Aaron.'" So Pharaoh thought that he was seeking help from the magicians against the Messenger of God, the Knower of secrets, but he was disappointed and lost Paradise and deserved Hell. And Pharaoh said, 'Bring me every learned magician.' So when the magicians came, Moses said to them, 'Throw down what you are going to throw down.' He only said that to them because when they lined up and were promised by Pharaoh to be brought near and given abundantly, They said, 'O Moses, either you throw down or we will be the first to throw down.' He said, 'Rather, throw down.' So Moses wanted them to start so that the people would see. What they did, then the truth comes after it and destroys their falsehood. And for this reason when they cast, they bewitched the eyes of the people and terrified them and produced a great magic. “So Moses felt fear within himself. What they have made is only the trick of a magician, and the magician will not succeed wherever he comes. ’” Then Moses said when they cast: “What you have brought is magic.
