10:83: God Almighty tells us that none believed in Moses, peace be upon him, despite the clear signs, decisive arguments, and shining proofs that he brought, except a few of the people of Pharaoh, from among the offspring, who were the youth, fearful and apprehensive of him and his people, lest they return to their former state of disbelief, because Pharaoh, may God curse him, was a stubborn tyrant, excessive in rebellion and insolence, and he had power and awe that his subjects feared him greatly. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: None believed in Moses except a few of his people, out of fear of Pharaoh and his people, lest he should tempt them. He said: The offspring who believed in Moses were from people other than the Children of Israel, from the people of Pharaoh, a few of them were Pharaoh’s wife, the believer of Pharaoh’s family, Pharaoh’s treasurer, and his treasurer’s wife. Ali bin Abi Talha narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: None believed in Moses except a few of his people, he said: the Children of Israel. According to Ibn Abbas, Ad-Dahhak, and Qatadah: the few offspring. Mujahid said regarding his statement: Except for the offspring of his people. He said: They are the children to whom Moses was sent long ago and whose fathers died. Ibn Jarir chose Mujahid’s statement that the offspring are from the Children of Israel, not from the people of Pharaoh, because the pronoun refers back to the closest of those mentioned. There is a consideration in this, because he meant by the offspring the young men and youth, and that they are from the Children of Israel. It is well known that all the Children of Israel believed in Moses, peace be upon him, and were gladdened by him. They knew his description and attributes and the glad tidings of him from their previous books, and that God Almighty would save them from the captivity of Pharaoh and make them victorious over him. For this reason, when this reached Pharaoh, he was very cautious and did not find anything wrong with him. When Moses came, Pharaoh harmed them severely. They said, ‘We were harmed before you came to us and after you came to us.’ He said, ‘Perhaps your Lord will destroy your enemy and make you successors in the land and see how you will act.’ If this is established, how can what is meant be anyone other than the descendants of Moses’ people, who are the Children of Israel, for fear of Pharaoh and his chiefs, meaning the nobles of his people, that he would tempt them? There was no one among the Children of Israel who feared that he would tempt them away from the faith except Qarun, for he was from the people of Moses and transgressed against them, but he was attached to Pharaoh, connected to him and clinging to his ropes. Whoever says that the pronoun in his saying and their chiefs refers to Pharaoh and the greatness of the king because of his following, or by deleting the family of Pharaoh and placing the complement in its place, has gone far, even though Ibn Jarir narrated it from some Grammarians. What indicates that there was no one among the Children of Israel except a believer is the Almighty’s saying:
10:84: God Almighty says, informing us about Moses, that he said to the Children of Israel: O my people, if you have believed in God, then rely on Him, if you should be Muslims. That is, God is sufficient for whoever relies on Him. Is not God sufficient for His servant? "And whoever relies on God - then He is sufficient for him." God Almighty often links worship and reliance, as in His saying: "So worship Him and rely on Him. Say, 'He is the Most Gracious. We have believed in Him, and in Him we rely.' Lord of the East and the West. There is no god but He, so take Him as Disposer of affairs." God Almighty commanded the believers to say in all their prayers many times: "You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help." The Children of Israel complied with that and said: "In God we have relied. Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people." That is, do not let them gain control over us and have power over us, so that they think that they have been given power only because they are on the truth and we are on falsehood, so that they are tempted by that. This is how it was narrated from Abu Majlaz and Abu Ad-Duha. Ibn Abi Nujayh and others said from Mujahid, no. We were not punished by the hands of Pharaoh’s people, nor by a punishment from You. Pharaoh’s people would say, If they were on the truth, they would not have been punished, nor would We have given them power over them, so that they would be tested by us. Abd al-Razzaq said, Ibn Uyaynah informed us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people, do not give them power over us, so that they would test us. And His statement, And save us by Your mercy, means deliver us by Your mercy and kindness, from the disbelieving people, meaning those who disbelieved in the truth and concealed it, and we have believed in You and put our trust in You.

10:87: The Almighty mentions the reason for saving the Children of Israel from Pharaoh and his people and how they were saved from them, and that is that God Almighty commanded Moses and his brother Aaron, peace be upon them, to take up residence, that is, to make houses for their people in Egypt. The commentators differed regarding the meaning of the Almighty’s saying: And make your houses places of prayer. Al-Thawri and others said on the authority of Khasif on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And make your houses places of prayer. He said: They were commanded to make them mosques. Al-Thawri also said on the authority of Ibn Mansur on the authority of Ibrahim, And make your houses places of prayer. He said: They were afraid, so they were commanded to pray in their houses. Mujahid, Abu Malik, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, Al-Dahhak, Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam, and his father Zaid bin Aslam said the same. And it seems that this, and God knows best, is because when the affliction from Pharaoh and his people became severe upon them and they were oppressed, they were commanded to pray frequently, as God Almighty said: O you who have believed, seek help through patience and prayer. And in the hadith, when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was distressed by something, he prayed. Narrated by Abu David, and for this reason the Almighty said in this verse: And make your houses places of prayer and establish prayer and give good tidings to the believers meaning the reward and imminent victory. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas in his interpretation of this verse: The Children of Israel said to Moses, peace be upon him, we cannot openly pray with the Pharaohs, so God permitted them to pray in their houses and they were commanded to make their houses facing the Qiblah. Mujahid said: And make your houses places of prayer when the Children of Israel feared that Pharaoh would kill them in the congregational churches, they were commanded to make their houses mosques facing the Kaaba and to pray in them secretly. Qatada and Al-Dahhak said the same. Saeed bin Jubair said: And make your houses places of prayer meaning facing each other.
10:88: This is a report from God Almighty about what Moses, peace be upon him, called upon Pharaoh and his people to do when they refused to accept the truth and continued in their misguidance and disbelief, stubbornly denying injustice, haughtiness, arrogance and insolence. Moses said: Our Lord, indeed You have given Pharaoh and his chiefs adornment meaning the furnishings and pleasures of this world and wealth meaning abundant and plentiful in this worldly life, our Lord, that they may go astray from Your way with the opening of the ya’ meaning You gave them that and You know that they will not believe in what You sent me with to them, as a lure from You, as in the saying of God Almighty: To test them therein and others read with the dammah of the ya’ meaning so that whoever You will of Your creation may be tempted by what You have given them, so that whoever You have led astray may think that You have only given them this because of Your love for them and Your care for them. Our Lord, obliterate their wealth Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: meaning destroy it. Ad-Dahhak, Abu Al-Aaliyah and Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas said: God made it into engraved stones as it was, and He said: Qatada told us that their crops turned into stones, and Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi said that their sugar turned into stones. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ismail bin Abi Al-Harith told us, Yahya bin Abi Bakr told us, on the authority of Abu Ma`shar, Muhammad bin Qais told me that Muhammad bin Ka`b recited Surah Yunus to Umar bin Abdul Aziz until he reached, And Moses said, ‘Our Lord, indeed You have given Pharaoh and his establishment splendor and wealth in the life of this world,’ until His saying, Our Lord, obliterate their wealth, the verse. Umar said: O Abu Hamza, what is obliteration? He said: All their wealth has turned into stones. Umar bin Abdul Aziz said to his servant: Bring me a bag. So he brought him a bag, and in it were chickpeas and eggs surrounded by stones. And His saying: And harden their hearts Ibn Abbas said: meaning, seal them so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment. This supplication was from Moses, peace be upon him, out of anger for God and His religion against Pharaoh and his people, who it became clear to him were no good and that nothing would come from them, just as Noah, peace be upon him, supplicated and said: “My Lord, do not leave on the earth from the disbelievers a single dwelling. If You leave them, they will mislead Your servants and will not give birth to anyone but wicked disbelievers.” For this reason, God Almighty responded to Moses, peace be upon him, regarding them, in which his brother Aaron responded to them, so God Almighty said: Your supplication has been answered. Abu Al-Aaliyah, Abu Salih, Ikrimah, Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi, and Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said: Moses supplicated and Aaron responded, meaning, We have responded, as in what you asked about the destruction of Pharaoh’s people. This verse may be used as evidence by those who say: The amen of the follower to the recitation of Al-Fatihah is equivalent to its recitation, because Moses supplicated and Aaron responded, and God Almighty said: Your supplication has been answered, so stand firm verse, meaning, just as your supplication has been answered, so stand firm in My affair. Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: So be upright and carry out my command, which is uprightness. Ibn Jurayj said: They say that Pharaoh remained after this call for forty years, and Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn said forty days.

10:90: The Almighty mentions how He drowned Pharaoh and his soldiers. When the Children of Israel left Egypt in the company of Moses, peace be upon him, and they were, as it was said, six hundred thousand fighters, in addition to their offspring, and they had borrowed a lot of jewelry from the Copts and left with them, Pharaoh’s anger at them intensified, so he sent gatherers to the cities to gather his soldiers from his provinces. He rode behind them with great pomp and huge armies for what God Almighty wanted for them, and no one who had power and authority in the rest of his kingdom stayed behind. They caught up with them at sunrise. So when the two hosts saw each other, the companions of Moses said, ‘Indeed, we are overtaken.’ That is because when they reached the shore of the sea and Pharaoh was behind them, and all that remained was for the two hosts to fight, the companions of Moses, peace be upon him, insisted on asking him how to be saved from what we were in? He said: I have been commanded to walk here. No indeed, my Lord is with me, and He will guide me. When the matter became difficult, it became easy, so God Almighty commanded him to strike the sea with his staff, so he struck it and the sea split, and each part was like a huge mountain, and there were twelve paths for each tribe. God commanded the wind, so it dried up its land. So strike for them a dry path in the sea, fearing no overtaking, nor being afraid. The water split between the paths like windows so that each people could see the others, lest they think they were lost. The Children of Israel crossed the sea, and when the last of them came out of it, Pharaoh and his soldiers reached its edge on the other side, and he was one hundred thousand dark-black, in addition to the rest of the colors. When he saw that, he was terrified and held back and was afraid, and he intended to return, but there was no time for escape. The fate was carried out, and the prayer was answered. And Gabriel, peace be upon him, came on a thin, rough horse and passed by Pharaoh’s horse, so it neighed at him and Gabriel stormed into the sea, and the horse stormed after him, and Pharaoh was not left with anything of himself, so he was patient with his commanders and said to them, The Children of Israel have no more right to the sea than we do. So they stormed in, all of them, and Michael was at the rear, not leaving anyone of them without attaching him to them. When they were in the middle of it and were the first to leave it, God Almighty ordered the sea to crash into them, and it crashed into them, and none of them escaped, and the waves began to raise them up and lower them, and the waves piled up over Pharaoh, and the throes of death overcame him, so he said while he was in that state: I believe that there is no god except that in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of the Muslims. So he believed when faith would not benefit him. “But when they saw Our punishment, they said, ‘We believe in God alone and disbelieve in that which we used to associate with Him.’ So their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our punishment. This is the way of God which has passed with His servants, and there the disbelievers lost out.” That is why God Almighty said in response to Pharaoh when he said what he said: Now, when you have disobeyed before, meaning, is this the time you say, and you have disobeyed God before this, between you and Him, and you were among the corrupters, meaning, on earth, those who led people astray, and We made them leaders calling to the Fire, and on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped. This that God Almighty related about Pharaoh, from his saying this in that state, is one of the secrets of the unseen that God informed His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, about. For this reason, Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may God have mercy on him, said: Sulayman ibn Harb told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Ali ibn Zayd, on the authority of Yusuf ibn Mihran, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When Pharaoh said, ‘I believe that there is no god except the one in whom the Children of Israel believe,’ he said, “Gabriel said to me: ‘If you had seen me, when I took from the sea and put it in his mouth, fearing that mercy would reach him.’” It was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim in their commentaries on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, and Al-Tirmidhi said: It is a good hadith. Abu Dawud Al-Tayalisi said: Shu’bah narrated to us on the authority of Adi bin Thabit and Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Gabriel said to me, ‘If you could see me taking from the mud of the sea and putting it in Pharaoh’s mouth for fear that mercy would reach him.’ Abu ‘Isa Al-Tirmidhi also narrated it, and Ibn Jarir also narrated it from other chains of transmission on the authority of Shu’bah, and he mentioned something similar. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is good, strange, and authentic. It was included in a narration by Ibn Jarir on the authority of Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna on the authority of Ghundar on the authority of Shu’bah on the authority of Ata’ and Adi on the authority of Saeed on the authority of Ibn Abbas, one of them traced it back to the Prophet, but it is as if the other did not trace it back, and God knows best. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashja’ narrated to us, Abu Khalid Al-Ahmar narrated to us on the authority of Umar bin Abdullah bin Ya’la Al-Thaqafi on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When God drowned Pharaoh, he pointed with his finger and raised his voice, I believe that there is no god except the One in Whom I believe. “He said: Gabriel feared that God’s mercy would overtake his anger, so he began to take hold of the camel with his wings and strike it in the face and throw it at him. This is how Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Sufyan ibn Wakee’ on the authority of Abu Khalid, with a chain of transmission ending with him. It was also narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, so Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us on the authority of Anbasa, who is Ibn Abi Saeed, on the authority of Katheer ibn Zadhan on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Gabriel said to me: O Muhammad, if you could see me covering him and putting some of the camel in his mouth for fear that God’s mercy would reach him and forgive him,” meaning Pharaoh. This Katheer ibn Zadhan, Ibn Ma’een said: I do not know him. Abu Zur’ah and Abu Hatim said: He is unknown, and the rest of his men are trustworthy. This hadith was transmitted by a group of the Salaf, including Qatada, Ibrahim al-Taymi, and Maymun ibn Mihran. It was narrated from Ad-Dahhak ibn Qays that he delivered a sermon with this to the people, and God knows best. And His statement: So this day We will save you with your body that you may be a sign to those who come after you, Ibn Abbas and others from the Salaf said: Some of the Children of Israel doubted the death of Pharaoh, so God the Almighty commanded the sea to throw him with his body intact, without a soul, and wearing his well-known armor on a high place of land, so that they would be certain of his death and destruction. For this reason God the Almighty said: So this day We will save you, meaning We will raise you up on a high place of land, with your body. Mujahid said: with your body. Al-Hasan said: with a body without a soul. Abdullah ibn Shaddad said: intact, meaning it was not torn apart, so that they would be certain of it and recognize it. Abu Sakhr said: with your armor. There is no contradiction between all of these statements, as mentioned above, and God knows best. And His statement: That it may be a sign to those who come after you means that it may be evidence for the Children of Israel of your death and destruction and that God is the All-Powerful, in Whose hand is the forelock of every creature, and that nothing can withstand His wrath. For this reason, some of them read: “That it may be a sign to those who come after you. And indeed, many of the people, of Our signs, are heedless.” That is, they do not learn from them or consider them. And their destruction was on the day of Ashura, as Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Ghundar told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina and the Jews were fasting on the day of Ashura. He said: What is this day that you are fasting? They said: This is the day on which Moses was victorious over Pharaoh. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his companions: You have more right to Moses than they do, so fast on it.

10:93: The Almighty tells us about the religious and worldly blessings He bestowed upon the Children of Israel. His saying: A place of truth is said to be the lands of Egypt and the Levant, which are next to Jerusalem and its environs. When God Almighty destroyed Pharaoh and his soldiers, the Mosaic state settled on the lands of Egypt in their entirety, as God Almighty said: "And We caused the people who were oppressed to inherit the eastern and western parts of the earth which We had blessed. And the good word of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel because they were patient. And We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people had made and what they had erected." And He said in the other verse: "So We brought them out of gardens and springs, and treasures and a noble station. Thus We caused them to inherit the Children of Israel." And He said: How many gardens and springs did they leave behind? The verses, but they continued with Moses, peace be upon him, seeking the lands of Jerusalem, which are the lands of Abraham, peace be upon him. Moses continued with those with him seeking Jerusalem, and there were a group of Amalekites in it, but the Children of Israel refrained from fighting them, so God Almighty scattered them in the wilderness for forty years, and Aaron died in it, then Moses. Peace be upon them, and after them they went out with Joshua bin Nun, and God opened for them the Holy House and their hands were established on it until Nebuchadnezzar took it from them for a period of time, then it returned to them, then the kings of Greece took it and it was under their rule for a long time, and God sent Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him, during that period, so the Jews, may God curse them, sought help from the kings of Greece to oppose Jesus, peace be upon him, and it was under their rule, and they slandered them and inspired them that this man would corrupt your subjects, so they sent someone to arrest him, so God raised him to Him, and some of the disciples resembled him to them by the will and destiny of God, so they took him and crucified him and believed that he was him, But they did not kill him for sure, but God raised him to Himself, and God is Exalted in Might and Wise. Then about three hundred years after Christ, peace be upon him, Constantine, one of the kings of Greece, entered the Christian religion, and he was a philosopher before that, so he entered the Christian religion, it was said as a precaution and it was said as a trick to corrupt it, so the bishops among them established laws and a law for him, which they invented and innovated, so he built for them churches, large and small synagogues, monasteries, temples, temples, and cells, and it spread Christianity was the religion of that time and became famous for its alteration, change, distortion, fabrication, lies, and opposition to the religion of Christ. Only a few monks remained who truly followed the religion of Christ, so they built monasteries for themselves in the wilderness, deserts, and wastelands. The Christians took control of the kingdom of the Levant, the Peninsula, and the lands of the Romans. This aforementioned king built the city of Constantinople, Qamamah, Bethlehem, and churches in the lands of Jerusalem, and the cities of Hawran, such as Busra, and other countries, huge, solid buildings. They worshipped the cross from that time on, and they reached the East and depicted churches. They permitted pork and other things that they had introduced from the branches and principles of their religion. They placed for him the lowly trust that they call the great one, and they classified laws for him. Explaining this would take a long time. The point is that their hand remained on this country until the Companions, may God be pleased with them, took it from them, and the conquest of Jerusalem was at the hands of the Commander of the Faithful, Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, and all praise and thanks be to God. His saying: And We provided them with good things means lawful, good, beneficial, and desirable provisions, both by nature and by law. His saying: And they did not differ until knowledge came to them means they did not differ on any of the issues except after knowledge came to them, meaning they did not have the right to differ, and God had made it clear to them and removed their confusion. It was mentioned in the hadith: “The Jews differed into seventy-one sects, and the Christians differed into seventy-two sects, and this nation will split into seventy-three sects, one of which will be in Paradise and seventy-two in Hell.” It was said: Who are they, O Messenger of God? He said: What I and my companions are upon. Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak with this wording, and it is in the Sunan and Musnads, and for this reason God Almighty said: Indeed, your Lord will judge between them meaning He will separate between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they differed.
10:94: Qatada bin Di'amah said: It has reached us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I do not doubt nor do I ask. Ibn Abbas, Saeed bin Jubair, and Al-Hasan Al-Basri said the same. This is to confirm for the nation and inform them that the description of their Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is present in the previous books in the hands of the People of the Book, as God the Almighty said: Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find written in what they have of the Torah and the Gospel (al-An'am 2:10). Then, with this knowledge that they know from their books as they know their own children, they distort it, change it, and do not believe in it, even though the proof has been established against them. For this reason God the Almighty said: Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe, even if every sign came to them, until they see the painful punishment. That is, they will not believe with a faith that benefits them, but rather when faith does not benefit a soul. For this reason, when Moses, peace be upon him, supplicated against Pharaoh and his people, he said: Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment. As God the Almighty said: "And even if We had sent down to them angels And the dead spoke to them, and We gathered together before them everything before. They would not believe unless God willed, but most of them are ignorant.” Then God Almighty said:

10:98: The Almighty says: “Was there not a village that believed in its perfection from the previous nations to whom We sent messengers? Rather, We did not send before you, O Muhammad, any messenger except that his people, or most of them, denied him, as the Almighty says: “Oh, the regret for the servants! There came not a messenger to them except that they mocked him.” Likewise, there came not a messenger to those before them except that they said, ‘A magician or a madman.’ “Likewise, We did not send before you a warner to a city except that its affluent ones said, ‘Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion, and we are following in their footsteps.’” And in the authentic hadith: “The prophets were presented to me, and the prophet would pass by with groups of people, and the prophet would pass by with one man, and the prophet would pass by with two men, and the prophet would not be with anyone.” Then he mentioned the large number of followers of Moses, peace be upon him, then he mentioned the large number of his nation, may the prayers and peace of God be upon him, a large number that filled the eastern and western horizons. The point is that there was no village that believed in its perfection from among the previous villages except the people of Yunus, who were the people of Nineveh, and their faith was nothing but…” Fearing the arrival of the punishment that their Messenger had warned them of after they had seen its causes, and their Messenger had left their midst, when they cried out to God and sought help from Him and beseeched Him and submitted to Him and brought their children, beasts and livestock and asked God Almighty to lift from them the punishment that their Prophet had warned them of, then God had mercy on them and removed the punishment from them and they were given a reprieve as God Almighty said: Except the people of Jonah, when they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world and gave them enjoyment for a time. The commentators differed as to whether the punishment of the Hereafter was removed from them along with the worldly punishment or was it only removed from them in this world? There are two opinions: One of them that it was only in the life of this world as is stated in this verse. The second in both of them is the saying of God the Almighty: “And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more. So they believed, and We gave them enjoyment for a time.” So He applied faith to them. And faith is a rescuer from the punishment of the Hereafter, and this is what is apparent, and God knows best. Qatada said in his interpretation of this verse: It did not benefit a village that disbelieved and then believed when the punishment came to it, and it was left behind, except the people of Yunus, when they lost their prophet and thought that the punishment had drawn near to them, God cast repentance into their hearts, and they put on sackcloth and separated every animal from its young, then they cried out to God for forty nights. So when God knew from them sincerity in their hearts and repentance and regret for what had happened from them, He removed the punishment from them after it had descended upon them. Qatada said: It was mentioned that the people of Yunus were in Nineveh, the land of Mosul. This was also narrated from Ibn Masoud, Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubair, and more than one of the Salaf. Ibn Masoud used to recite it: Why was there not a city that believed? Abu Imran said on the authority of Abu al-Jild, who said: When the punishment descended upon them, it began to circle around their heads like pieces of a dark night. So they went to one of their scholars and said: Teach us a supplication that we can make so that perhaps God will remove the punishment from us. He said: Say: O Ever-Living when there is no living, O Ever-Living, the Reviver of the dead, O Ever-Living, there is no god but You. He said: So the punishment was removed from them. 10:99: The Almighty says: And if your Lord had willed O Muhammad, He would have permitted all the people of the earth to believe in what you have brought them, and they would have all believed. But He has wisdom in what He does, as in His saying: "And if your Lord had willed, He could have made mankind one community; but they will not cease to differ. Except whom your Lord has given mercy - and for that He created them. And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together." And the Almighty says: "Have those who have believed not despaired that if God had willed, He could have guided all mankind?" For this reason the Almighty says: "Then would you compel mankind meaning would you force them and compel them until they become believers? meaning that is not upon you, nor upon you, but rather God He misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wills. So let not your soul perish in regret for them It is not upon you to guide them, but God guides whom He wills Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they do not believe Indeed, you do not guide whom you love Then upon you is only the conveyance, and upon Us is the account So remind, for you are only a reminder." * You have no control over them” and other verses indicating that God Almighty is the doer of whatever He wills, the guide of whomever He wills, the misguider of whomever He wills, due to His knowledge, wisdom, and justice. For this reason, God Almighty said: “And it is not for a soul to believe except by permission of God. And He places the uncleanness” which is corruption and misguidance upon those who do not reason meaning God’s arguments and proofs, and He is the just in all of that in guiding whomever He guides and misguiding whomever He misguides.

10:101: God Almighty guides His servants to reflect on His blessings and the dazzling signs that God has created in the heavens and the earth for those with understanding, including the bright stars in the heavens, fixed and moving, the sun and moon, the night and day and their differences and the insertion of one into the other until this one becomes long and that one becomes short, then this one becomes short and that one becomes long, the height of the sky and its vastness and its beauty and its adornment and what God has sent down from it of rain, reviving the earth after its death, and bringing forth in it of various fruits, crops, flowers and types of plants and what He has sown in it of animals of different shapes, colors and benefits and what is in it of mountains, plains, deserts, civilization and ruins, and what is in the sea of wonders and waves and it is with this subjected and subdued for the travelers, carrying their ships and sailing them gently by the subjection of the Almighty. And His statement: Then do they await anything other than the days of those who passed on before them? That is, do these disbelievers in you, O Muhammad, await anything other than the days of God for those who passed on before them from the past nations who disbelieved in their messengers? “Say, ‘Then wait, for I am with you among those who wait. Then We will save Our messengers and those who have believed.’” That is, and We will destroy those who disbelieved in the messengers. Thus is it incumbent upon Us to save the believers. That is, it is a right that God Almighty has made obligatory upon His noble self, like His statement: Your Lord has prescribed mercy upon Himself. And as it came in the two Sahihs on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “Indeed, God has written a book and it is with Him above the Throne: ‘My mercy prevails over My wrath.’”

10:104: God Almighty says to His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, "O people, if you are in doubt about the truth of what I have brought you of the true religion which God has revealed to me, then I do not worship those you worship besides God, but I worship God alone, with no partner for Him. It is He who takes your souls as He gave you life, and then to Him is your return. But if your gods which you call upon besides God are true, then I do not worship them, so call upon them, but let them harm me, for they neither harm nor benefit. The One in whose hand is harm and benefit is God alone, with no partner for Him. And I have been commanded to be among the believers. His statement, And set your face toward the religion, inclining toward truth," the verse, means that I should devote my worship to God alone, inclining toward truth, meaning deviating from polytheism. For this reason He said, "And do not be among the polytheists, which is conjoined with His statement, And I have been commanded to be among the believers." And His saying, And if God should touch you with harm, the verse explains that good and evil, benefit and harm, are only due to God Almighty alone, no one shares that with Him. He is the One Who deserves to be worshipped alone, with no partner. Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir narrated in the biography of Safwan bin Saleem, on the authority of Abdullah bin Wahb, that Yahya bin Ayoub informed me, on the authority of Isa bin Musa, on the authority of Safwan bin Saleem, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Seek goodness throughout your life and expose yourselves to the breezes of your Lord, for God has breezes of His mercy with which He afflicts whomever He wills of His servants. And ask Him to cover your faults and calm your fears.” Then he narrated it on the authority of Al-Layth, on the authority of Isa bin Musa, on the authority of Safwan, on the authority of a man from Ashja’, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, with a similar chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And His saying, And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful, means for whoever repents to Him and puts his trust in Him, even from any sin, even from associating partners with Him, then He will accept his repentance.
